quotes.text: A metric that requires interpretation isn't a metric. It's a conversation starter that sounds collaborative. It's also why decisions take weeks.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Captures the episode's core critique of interpretable metrics in one sharp line.

quotes.text: Visibility is observation. Control is obligation. And Microsoft's ecosystem for all its branding doesn't magically fix that.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Draws the key distinction between dashboards and real control.

quotes.text: If a KPI turns red and nothing happens until the next meeting, it's not a KPI. It's a mood indicator.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: A memorable test for whether a KPI actually drives action.

quotes.text: the thing most people miss is that self-service is not the enemy. Ungoverned self-service is. Self-service on top of a controlled semantic layer is fine. That's just people asking questions.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Gives a balanced, practical position on self-service BI.

quotes.text: AI does not belong in the rule engine. It belongs in three places. Explanation, summarization, and option generation.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Sets a clear boundary for where probabilistic AI fits in decision systems.

takeaways: A KPI only earns leadership attention when it carries an obligation: a precise trigger, one accountable owner, a pre-committed action, a time window and a feedback loop.

Build the decision stack in layers: converged data in Fabric and OneLake, governed meaning in the semantic model, decision state in Dataverse, enforcement with Power Automate and access through Copilot Studio.
Keep the decision core deterministic and use AI only for explanation, summarization and option generation, never for triggering escalations or changing operational state.
hook: Executives keep asking for every KPI on one page, and teams keep building dashboards that get ignored two weeks later. This episode is for BI leads, architects and finance or IT leaders who want to turn KPIs into enforced decision rules on the Microsoft stack. You will learn how to cut decision latency with triggers, owners, actions, time windows and a decision ledger.
